hints: Focus on the two different Group 2 trends here, thermal stability of carbonates and nitrates goes one way down the group, while solubilities go different ways for sulfates and hydroxides.
Remember that larger cations down the group polarise large anions less, so carbonates and nitrates get more stable from magnesium to barium.
Now compare solubilities, sulfates get less soluble down the group while hydroxides get more soluble, so check which pair follows that pattern.
walkthrough:
**Recall the thermal stability trend**

Think big cation, gentle pull. Down Group 2 the ion gets larger and less polarising, so it distorts the carbonate or nitrate ion less.

Decomposition examples:
$$\text{MCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MO} + \text{CO}_2$$
$$2\text{M}(\text{NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

**Apply it to options A and D**

Stability increases down the group: $\text{Mg} < \text{Ca} < \text{Sr} < \text{Ba}$. So barium compounds need a higher temperature to decompose than strontium or calcium compounds.

**Recall the two solubility trends**

This is the classic split students must memorise. For sulfates, solubility decreases down the group. For hydroxides, solubility increases down the group.

In short:
$$\text{MgSO}_4 \text{ (soluble)} > ... > \text{BaSO}_4 \text{ (insoluble)}$$
$$\text{Mg}(\text{OH})_2 \text{ (least soluble)} < ... < \text{Ba}(\text{OH})_2 \text{ (most soluble)}$$

**Pick the correct statement**

Barium sulfate is near the insoluble end while magnesium sulfate is very soluble, so barium sulfate is less soluble. That matches one trend perfectly, while the other three statements state the opposite of the true trends.

options.A: Incorrect. Carbonate thermal stability increases down Group 2 because the larger $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ ion polarises the $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ ion less than $\text{Sr}^{2+}$ does. So barium carbonate is more thermally stable than strontium carbonate, not less.
options.B: Correct. Group 2 sulfate solubility decreases down the group. $\text{MgSO}_4$ is very soluble in water while $\text{BaSO}_4$ is essentially insoluble, so barium sulfate is less soluble than magnesium sulfate.
options.C: Incorrect. Group 2 hydroxide solubility increases down the group. $\text{Ca}(\text{OH})_2$ is more soluble than $\text{Mg}(\text{OH})_2$, which is almost insoluble. This option reverses the trend.
options.D: Incorrect. Nitrate thermal stability also increases down Group 2 for the same polarising power reason as carbonates. So calcium nitrate is less thermally stable than strontium nitrate, not more.
